issues.body:
Line 987 builds `f"repos/{registry_repo}/git/trees/{worker_pr.LEDGER_REF}?recursive=1"`. The old read placed the ref in the query string; in path position, a value containing `?` or `#` can now rewrite the query — e.g. `REGISTRY_LEDGER_REF="ledger?recursive=0&x="` would drop recursion.

Still a nit, unchanged from round 2: LEDGER_REF is operator-supplied workflow configuration (worker-pr.py:418), not untrusted input, and the outcome fails CLOSED anyway — a non-recursive tree lists only top-level entries, nothing starts with `orchestration/provenance/`, and the new presence guard raises. Noted only because scripts/pat-validity.py already quotes this same constant with `urllib.parse.quote(LEDGER_REF, safe='')`, so this line diverges from an established in-repo pattern.
issues.fix_hint: Match pat-validity.py: `f"repos/{registry_repo}/git/trees/{urllib.parse.quote(worker_pr.LEDGER_REF, safe='')}?recursive=1"` (add the `urllib.parse` import if absent). The endpoint-wiring self-test pins the default `ledger`, which quotes to itself, so it stays green.
issues.title: `worker_pr.LEDGER_REF` is interpolated into path position without URL quoting, diverging from pat-validity.py's house style

issues.body:
Every fixture in the new block either yields a non-empty result or is expected to raise. Nothing asserts the third outcome the function must support: the provenance directory EXISTS on the ledger but holds no record for THIS repo (in production, a ledger carrying only `orchestration/provenance/README.md` plus other repos' records), which must return an empty set quietly.

The code is correct today — README.md satisfies `any(path.startswith(prefix))` and the loop matches nothing — and I confirmed `orchestration/provenance/README.md` is tracked, so the guard cannot mis-fire in steady state. But the property is unpinned: moving the guard after the loop as `if not numbers: raise` keeps the `{685}` check and the renamed-directory check both green while turning a genuinely-empty census into a fatal one. Since this raise is the fix for round-1 major #2, its boundary is worth one line.
issues.fix_hint:
Add one case asserting the quiet-empty outcome:

    check("...and a present-but-empty provenance directory reads as 'nothing recorded'",
          recorded_pr_numbers(repo, "reg/istry", worker_pr,
                              read_tree=lambda: {"truncated": False,
                                                 "tree": [{"path": "orchestration/provenance/README.md",
                                                           "type": "blob"}]}),
          set())

This distinguishes "the directory is gone" (raise) from "the directory is there and empty" (set()) — exactly the pair the new guard exists to separate.
issues.title: The legitimate "directory present, zero records" outcome returns set() but is not pinned, so the new presence guard could be tightened into a false fail-closed unnoticed

verdict.summary:
Round 3 re-review of the same tree as round 2 (HEAD b35c524ea, one fix commit; no new work landed since). The change is correct, fail-closed, and its self-test is non-vacuous. I re-verified every mutation the round-2 approval rested on against the checkout rather than the diff text.

CORRECTNESS. `recorded_pr_numbers` (scripts/mint-provenance.py:970-1005) now reads the whole ledger tree via `git/trees/{ref}?recursive=1` and slices names with `prefix = PROVENANCE_DIR + '/'` derived from the production builder (worker-pr.py:2673-2675, PROVENANCE_DIR='orchestration/provenance'). Three ordered guards separate "could not tell" from "nothing recorded": non-dict-or-truncated raises, non-list `tree` raises, and absent provenance directory raises. The caller at :914-916/:929 is inside `census`, which propagates MintError — an unreadable population hard-fails the census instead of being reported as empty. That is the correct direction for a trust-plane reader.

This strictly improves on the old read: `contents/{dir}` silently caps at 1000 entries with no truncation signal, so as the ledger grows the previous code would have started under-reporting recorded PRs (fail-OPEN, re-minting over existing records). The new read fails closed instead. Whole-tree truncation is a real but distant limit (7MB / ~100k entries; the tracked directory holds 34 records today), and it raises rather than lies when reached — observation, not a defect.

TEST VALIDITY. Each new assertion reds on the mutation it exists for: drop the truncated clause -> "no raise" (:1834-1842); drop the isinstance-dict guard -> the `None` fixture raises AttributeError, uncaught, self-test crashes (:1843-1853); drop the list guard -> TypeError on `any()` over None (:1854-1862); drop the presence guard -> the renamed-directory case returns set() and hits the else branch (:1863-1874).
